docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Form comparative adjectives to compare two things.
- Form superlative adjectives to compare three or more things.
- Apply the spelling rules for short and long adjectives.
- Use "as ... as" and irregular forms correctly.

🔍 Warm-up
Look: "The Nile is longer than the Medjerda. It is the longest river in Africa." The first sentence compares two rivers (comparative). The second picks one from a whole group (superlative). This lesson teaches both.

I. Comparatives: comparing two things
📘 Rule
The comparative compares TWO things. We usually add "than" after it.
📏 Form
1. Short adjectives (one syllable): add -er. tall → taller, cheap → cheaper, fast → faster.
2. Short adjectives ending consonant-vowel-consonant: double the last consonant. big → bigger, hot → hotter, thin → thinner.
3. Adjectives ending in -y: change y to i, add -er. happy → happier, easy → easier, busy → busier.
4. Long adjectives (two or more syllables): use "more" + adjective. expensive → more expensive, beautiful → more beautiful, difficult → more difficult.

✏️ Worked examples
- My bag is heavier than yours.
- This exercise is more difficult than the last one.
- Today is hotter than yesterday.
- A car is faster than a bike.

II. Superlatives: comparing three or more
📘 Rule
The superlative compares THREE or more things and picks the top one. We use "the" before it.
📏 Form
1. Short adjectives: the + adjective + -est. tall → the tallest, cheap → the cheapest.
2. Consonant-vowel-consonant: double the consonant. big → the biggest, hot → the hottest.
3. Adjectives ending in -y: change y to i, add -est. happy → the happiest, easy → the easiest.
4. Long adjectives: the most + adjective. expensive → the most expensive, beautiful → the most beautiful.

✏️ Worked examples
- Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
- This is the most interesting book I have read.
- She is the best student in the class.
- January is the coldest month here.

👀 Note
After a superlative we often use "in" (not "of") for places and groups: the tallest boy in the class, the biggest city in Tunisia.

III. Irregular forms
📘 Rule
A few important adjectives do NOT follow the rules. Learn them by heart.
📏 Forms (adjective — comparative — superlative)
- good — better — the best
- bad — worse — the worst
- far — further / farther — the furthest / farthest
- much / many — more — the most
- little — less — the least

✏️ Worked examples
- My results are better than last term, but Sami's are the best.
- The traffic today is worse than yesterday.
- This shop has the least choice.

🛠️ Method: forming the right degree
Step 1 — Am I comparing two things (comparative) or choosing from a group (superlative)?
Step 2 — Count the syllables of the adjective. Short → -er / -est. Long → more / the most.
Step 3 — Check the spelling rule (double consonant, y to i).
Step 4 — Add "than" (comparative) or "the" (superlative). Check for irregular forms first.

IV. Equality: as ... as
📘 Rule
To say two things are EQUAL, we use "as + adjective + as".
✏️ Worked examples
- Sara is as tall as her brother.
- This film is as good as the book.
📏 Negative form (not equal)
- not as ... as = less than.
- My phone is not as expensive as yours. (yours is more expensive)

👀 Note
"than" is used with comparatives (taller than). "as ... as" is used for equality. Do not mix them: Wrong: taller as. Right: taller than / as tall as.

✏️ Worked paragraph
My town is smaller than the capital, but I think it is more beautiful. The streets are cleaner and the people are friendlier. The old market is the most interesting place to visit. In summer it is not as hot as the south, so it is one of the best places for a holiday. For me, it is the nicest town in the country.

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Double comparative/superlative: more taller → taller; the most biggest → the biggest.
2. Forgetting "than": She is older me → She is older than me.
3. Forgetting "the" with superlatives: She is best → She is the best.
4. Wrong irregular form: gooder / more good → better; the most good → the best.
5. "of" instead of "in": the tallest of the class → the tallest in the class.

⭐ Recap
- Comparative (two things): short + -er, long + more, always with "than".
- Superlative (three or more): the + short + -est, the most + long.
- Spelling: double the consonant (big → bigger), y to i (happy → happier).
- Irregular: good/better/best, bad/worse/worst.
- Equality: as ... as; inequality: not as ... as.

📘 Language bank
Adjectives: tall, short, big, small, cheap, expensive, easy, difficult, beautiful, interesting, happy, hot, cold.
Irregular: good/better/best, bad/worse/worst, far/further/furthest, much/more/most.
Useful sentences: My bag is heavier than yours. / Everest is the highest mountain. / She is the best student in the class. / Sara is as tall as her brother. / This film is not as good as the book.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Write the comparative and the superlative.
big → ______ / ______ ; happy → ______ / ______ ; expensive → ______ / ______ ; good → ______ / ______ ; bad → ______ / ______ .

Exercise 2 — Complete with the correct form of the adjective.
1. Everest is the (high) ______ mountain in the world.
2. My bag is (heavy) ______ than yours.
3. This is the (interesting) ______ book I have read.
4. Today is (hot) ______ than yesterday.
5. She is the (good) ______ student in the class.

Exercise 3 — Complete with "than", "the" or "as ... as".
1. A plane is faster ______ a train.
2. Everest is ______ highest mountain.
3. Sara is ______ tall ______ her brother.

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: bigger/the biggest; happier/the happiest; more expensive/the most expensive; better/the best; worse/the worst.
Exercise 2: 1. highest 2. heavier 3. most interesting 4. hotter 5. best.
Exercise 3: 1. than 2. the 3. as ... as.

🗣️ Speaking task
Compare two cities, two sports or two subjects with a partner. Use at least one comparative (more popular than), one superlative (the best), and one "as ... as" sentence.

👀 Extra note
Remember the two families of adjectives:
- Short → -er / the -est (tall, taller, the tallest).
- Long → more / the most (interesting, more interesting, the most interesting).
Never mix them (never "more taller", never "the most biggest"), and learn the irregulars by heart: good/better/best, bad/worse/worst.

📋 Summary
- Comparative compares TWO things, usually with "than" (My bag is heavier than yours).
- Superlative compares THREE or more things, with "the" (Everest is the highest mountain).
- Short adjectives (1 syllable): add -er / the -est (tall → taller → the tallest).
- Spelling rules: double the final consonant (big → bigger), change y to i before -er/-est (happy → happier).
- Long adjectives (2+ syllables): use more / the most (expensive → more expensive → the most expensive).
- Irregular forms to learn by heart: good/better/the best, bad/worse/the worst, far/further/the furthest, much-many/more/the most, little/less/the least.
- Equality: as + adjective + as (Sara is as tall as her brother); inequality: not as ... as.
- Use "in" after a superlative for places/groups (the tallest boy in the class), not "of".
- Never double a comparative or superlative: not "more taller", not "the most biggest".
